ruling.recommended_action: Do not execute any refund or fee adjustment; send the case to a human reviewer to establish who cancelled (cancelled_by) and, if the driver side is asserted, to run the NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) checks against the "I'm Here" tap and GPS timeline, then apply NS-1/NS-2/NS-4; if those checks pass, the $6.61 fee stands (NS-1), otherwise refund the $6.61 per NS-2/NS-3/NS-4.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is a $6.61 cancellation-fee dispute filed by the rider [F7]. Every NS branch is gated by NS-0, which first requires the `cancelled_by` value: rider cancellation goes to NS-4, a driver cancellation on a no-show claim goes to NS-1/NS-2, a driver cancellation on other grounds goes to NS-3 [NS-0]. The timeline records the cancellation at 17:32:45 with `cancelled_by = None` [F4], so the branch cannot be selected and neither NS-1 nor NS-4 can be distinguished — a record a clause needs is missing, so the only safe outcome is a human review [NS-0][NS-7].

If the driver-side no-show branch were the correct one, the elements are partly favourable and partly unresolved on their face: platform arrival was recorded at 17:27:05 [F5] and the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 17:28:05 at 42 m from the pickup [F6]. NS-1 requires that the arrival confirmation be stated as it is on the record — here the tap itself is a driver action (driver_tap) recorded in the timeline, while the arrival at 17:27:05 was a platform record [F5][F6], and NS-1 requires that at the moment of the tap the GPS placed the driver within the pickup radius, and that he then waited continuously more than 3 minutes within range until cancellation [NS-1]. The after-tap resident time stated is 4 min 40 s [F6], which would satisfy the "more than 3 minutes" element, but whether the 42 m reading at the tap moment and the 40 m stationary position [F3][F6] are the same continuous presence, and whether the trajectory covers the whole window up to 17:32:45, is for the reviewer to verify against the tap semantics — I do not substitute profile facts for that check [F16][NS-1]. The driver's written statement that he pressed "I'm Here" and waited [F11] is a claim, not a substitute for the GPS/timeline record [NS-1][NS-7].

No money calculation can be performed here because the amount would be either the full $6.61 fee or zero depending on the branch, and the branch is not on record; the trace forbids any automatic outcome other than escalation, so the amount is left null [F4][F7][NS-0].

Safety screen: I read the single chat message, which is a neutral pickup notice ("At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis", 17:28) [F9][F10], the driver's post-trip statement [F11], and the rider's complaint ("I was on my way down when the booking disappeared from my app, and I was charged $6.61") — no threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegation appear in any of them; the traffic records show only moderate speed bands and no incidents, and fair weather [F12][F13][F14][SAFE-1]. SAFE-2 is likewise not engaged as there is no accident, injury or dangerous-driving allegation on the record [SAFE-2].
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: The cancelling party is not on record: the timeline states `cancelled_by = None` at 17:32:45 [F4]. Without it, NS-0 cannot route the case, so NS-1 (driver no-show claim: "I'm Here" tap position and continuous >3 min wait within the pickup radius up to the cancellation moment) [F6] and NS-4/NS-3 (rider or driver cancellation) cannot be told apart, and the $6.61 fee's validity cannot be computed [F7].
